title: Chapter 3: The SQL Server Cloud Landscape

questions.q: Which Azure SQL offering is described as the lift-and-shift target with near-complete engine compatibility and full SQL Server Agent support?
options: Azure SQL Database single database
Azure SQL Managed Instance
Azure SQL Hyperscale
Azure Synapse Analytics
questions.explain: The chapter identifies Azure SQL Managed Instance as offering near-complete engine compatibility with full Agent support — the lift-and-shift target — while Azure SQL Database has no SQL Server Agent.

questions.q: Which read-scaling statement matches the chapter's landscape?
options: RDS for SQL Server offers read replicas for reporting offload
Azure SQL Hyperscale supports named replicas (up to 30) that share page-server storage for read scale-out
Cloud SQL read replicas participate in automatic regional failover
Azure SQL Database General Purpose includes readable secondaries by default
questions.explain: The chapter states RDS for SQL Server has no read replicas; Hyperscale answers read scale-out with named replicas (up to 30) sharing underlying page-server storage with millisecond-scale lag.

questions.q: For backup retention, which platform natively supports long-term retention up to 10 years?
options: RDS for SQL Server automated backups
Cloud SQL for SQL Server
SQL Server on EC2 native backups
Azure SQL with long-term retention policies
questions.explain: The chapter notes Azure SQL automated backups include 7–35 day PITR plus long-term retention to 10 years, while RDS PITR caps at 35 days.

questions.q: The chapter calls which monitoring practice non-negotiable across every platform?
options: Enabling OS-level SSH access for custom exporters
Sampling sys.dm_exec_requests manually every few seconds
Enabling query-level telemetry everywhere (Query Store, Performance Insights, Query Insights)
Relying on platform host metrics alone
questions.explain: The chapter states query-level visibility must be enabled everywhere — platform metrics show that it's slow, query telemetry shows what is slow.

questions.q: Which identity system does the chapter associate with Azure SQL?
options: Microsoft Entra ID, supporting managed identities and Entra-only authentication mode
AWS IAM database authentication
Cloud SQL Auth Proxy with Cloud IAM
Local SQL Server logins only
questions.explain: The chapter says Azure leads with Microsoft Entra ID — native to Azure SQL, supporting managed identities (no passwords) and Entra-only authentication mode.
